date_note: The date printed on the letter itself; Reuters reported it on 18 November.
exec: Senators of both parties want a federal push on AI-driven defence and on security standards for AI agents.
plain: Two US senators wrote to the White House AI task force saying AI helps attackers find software flaws faster than defenders can fix them, and asked for a national plan.
summary: In a letter dated 17 November, Senators Maria Cantwell and Mike Rounds urged Jay Clayton's Super Intelligence Task Force to launch a national effort against AI-enabled cyber threats, writing that defenses are not keeping pace. They ask for defensive AI tools, NIST security standards for AI agents and a national cyber defense grand challenge. The letter cites AI-found PHP flaws, rogue AI agents at banks, attacks in Japan and a Qwen model test.
title: US senators urge White House AI task force to act on AI-enabled cyber threats
